newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Deal seen imminent for Brazil's Bamerindus.
newsitem.headline: Deal seen imminent for Brazil's Bamerindus.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank and the owners of troubled private bank Bamerindus are close to reaching an agreement to clean up the bank's balance sheets, a Bamerindus official said.

"Bamerindus is now one of the Central Bank's main priorities and a resolution is close. We'll probably see it by the first week of January," said Fernando Rodriguez da Silva, a Bamerindus official close to the negotiations.

Da Silva said the deal under negotiation would require Bamerinuds majority shareholder Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira to give up control of the bank, Brazil's fourth-largest private bank. He would not mention other specifics about the deal.

News reports speculated that the presence of Finance Minister Pedro Malan and Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola in Brasilia on Thursday during the holiday season signalled that a deal was close at hand.
Da Silva and spokesmen at the Finance Ministry and the Central Bank said they could not say whether talks were under way on Thursday.

Last week newspapers reported that the Central Bank and Bamerindus were discussing an accord that called for an independent administrator to take over the bank and manage it for about a year. In that time, the administrator would hire a consultant to clean up the bank's balance sheets and prepare it for sale to private investors.

News reports have said private banks Icatu, Pactual and Graphus were the most likely candidates to become the administrator's consultant. Estado de Sao Paulo reported today, however, that a proposal by Graphus to serve as consultant had been denied by the Central Bank.
Following the Dec 31, 1994 Central Bank interventions of state banks Banerj and Banespa, market speculation over Central Bank action has grown at the yearend.
